question: Which products have the lowest non-null days_of_supply on the latest snapshot?

days_of_supply.name: Mean stored days of supply
days_of_supply.description: Unweighted mean of stored days-of-supply values; not a demand forecast.
days_of_supply.temporal_semantics: One selected snapshot or separate exact snapshot_date groups; never combine balances across dates.
days_of_supply.null_handling: Non-null stored values only; SUM and AVG of no observations remain NULL; COUNT is zero; absent snapshots are not zero stock.
days_of_supply.zero_denominator: Return NULL using NULLIF; never substitute zero for an undefined ratio.

data.sql: SELECT i.snapshot_date AS snapshot_date, p.product_id AS product_id, p.product_name AS product_name, i.days_of_supply AS days_of_supply FROM commerce.inventory AS i JOIN commerce.products AS p ON i.product_id = p.product_id WHERE i.snapshot_date = (SELECT MAX(j.snapshot_date) FROM commerce.inventory AS j) AND i.days_of_supply IS NOT NULL ORDER BY i.days_of_supply ASC, p.product_id ASC LIMIT 200
limitations: Historical monthly observations; every answer must state the selected snapshot date.

Stored rate values are returned unchanged as fractions; 0.25 displays as 25 percent, without implying the original source formula.
Inventory observations are historical; selected snapshot dates: 2022-12-31

metadata.explanation: Retrieves products with the lowest non-null days_of_supply at the latest inventory snapshot. Joins inventory to products to get product details, filters for the maximum snapshot date and non-null days_of_supply, orders by days_of_supply ascending with product_id as a tie-breaker, and limits to 200 rows.
